title: Vampires and Dracula
passage:
A man stands before you. He is well-dressed and polite. However, there is something dark about him. When you try to look into a mirror, you cannot see his face. His name is Dracula, and he is the most famous vampire in history.

Stories of vampires as we know them date back to the early 18th century. During this time, there were many sick people and deaths that people could not explain. People would dig up the bodies to study what their deaths showed, and they found bodies that looked to be alive. Their bodies' hair and fingernails were longer. Their stomachs looked full, and there was dried blood near the corners of their mouths. People began hearing news of monsters coming out of the ground at night for a human buffet and then returning to their places at dawn.

In 1897, a man named Bram Stoker wrote Dracula. At the time, it did not get much attention, but in 1922, the movie Nosferatu was made. It was clear that they used Stoker's story to make this movie without asking him. This caused a giant fight between Stoker and the filmmakers. After this, Dracula was known by everyone and became the vampire we think of today.
